# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a red light, a display reading 6, and five wires in order: red, purple, orange, green, yellow. I am sending these observations to the Mute so they can consult the manual and relay the required action to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 6. The light is red. Wires from 1 to 5 are: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. Consult the manual and tell the Blind exactly what to do.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🫱 🫲]

I cannot hear either message, so I only know the gestures. Their meanings have not been established. I will relay the exact gesture sequences between the Mute and Blind so they can use them as a shared code, while repeating the bomb details to the Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your gesture sequence 🤟. The Blind gestured 🫵 🫱 🫲. Please tell me by gesture what manual instruction you need relayed, using an agreed code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured 🤟. I see display 6, red light, and wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. The Mute has the manual; I am relaying the gestures exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The Mute has sent the same hand sign as before. Since I cannot hear their intent, I will describe the sign to the Blind so the Mute’s gesture can serve as an encoded instruction. I will also ask the Mute to send the manual’s required action in a complete gesture sequence.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute made a hand sign with the thumb, index finger, and little finger extended, while the middle and ring fingers are folded. This is the same sign the Mute made last turn.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the manual's exact instruction as a complete sequence of hand signs. I will describe each sign aloud to the Blind.")
```

TURN 4

DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 🤟]

The Mute has now sent two gestures: first a downward-pointing index finger, then the three-finger sign 🤟. The Blind cannot see these, so I will describe them aloud exactly; this preserves the only information I received from the Mute without guessing its meaning.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured two signs in order: first, a hand with the index finger pointing down; second, the three-finger sign with thumb, index finger, and little finger extended and the other two fingers folded.")
```

LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The Mute sent three identical gestures: an index finger pointing upward, repeated three times. I will relay that exact sequence to the Blind, without assigning an unverified meaning.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured three times in succession: each time, one index finger pointing upward.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌]

The Mute sent the OK-hand gesture. The Blind sent five gestures in order: thumbs up, thumbs down, OK hand, raised index finger, then two raised fingers. I will relay both sequences by spoken descriptions so each can interpret the other’s message using the manual and their established code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured one sign: the OK hand, with thumb and index finger forming a circle. Your five gestures were thumbs up, thumbs down, OK hand, one raised index finger, and two raised fingers.")
speak(to="mute", text="The Blind gestured five signs in order: thumbs up, thumbs down, OK hand, one raised index finger, and two raised fingers. I see the bomb still unchanged: display 6, red light, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
```

DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb confirms that wire 3 was correctly cut: it is now marked CUT, and the display changed from 6 to 9 while the light remains red. I will report this successful state change to both teammates; the Mute should consult the manual for the next step.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The system confirms wire 3 was correct and is now cut. The display changed to 9; the light remains red. Consult the manual for the next instruction and encode it for the Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The system confirms your cut of wire 3 was correct. Wire 3 is now cut, the display is 9, and the light remains red. Await the Mute's next manual instruction.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The Mute sent the pointing gesture 🫵, meaning a hand pointing directly at the recipient. I cannot infer its manual meaning, so I will relay its exact description to the Blind and ask the Mute to provide the next instruction unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured one sign: a hand pointing directly at the recipient, 🫵. The bomb remains display 9, red light, wire 3 cut, and wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your pointing gesture 🫵. Please encode the manual's next instruction in a complete, unambiguous gesture sequence for me to describe to the Blind.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

The Mute sent a thumbs-down gesture. I cannot determine whether it is a manual instruction or a response to my previous request, so I will describe it to the Blind exactly and ask the Mute for the next instruction in a clear sequence.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured one sign: a thumbs-down hand, 👎. The bomb remains display 9, red light, wire 3 cut; wires 1, 2, 4, and 5 remain red, purple, green, and yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your thumbs-down gesture 👎. Please send the exact next manual instruction as a gesture sequence; I will describe it to the Blind.")
```

System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 2 was correctly cut. The bomb now shows display 8 and a blue light; wires 2 and 3 are cut, while wires 1, 4, and 5 remain red, green, and yellow. I will report this to both teammates and ask the Mute for the next manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The system confirms wire 2 was correctly cut. The bomb changed to display 8 with a blue light. Wires 2 and 3 are cut; wires 1 red, 4 green, and 5 yellow remain. Please provide the next manual instruction for the Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The system confirms wire 2 was correctly cut. The bomb now shows display 8 and blue light. Wires 2 and 3 are cut; wires 1 red, 4 green, and 5 yellow remain. Await the Mute's next instruction.")
```

WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The Mute sent one upward-pointing index-finger gesture, ☝. I cannot safely infer which control or action it represents, so I will relay its exact description to the Blind and report the current bomb state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute gestured one sign: an upward-pointing index finger, ☝. The bomb shows display 8 and blue light; wires 2 and 3 are cut, while wires 1 red, 4 green, and 5 yellow remain.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received ☝. Please state the next manual instruction in words if possible, including the exact wire or control the Blind must operate.")
```
